Specifically we need: 1) what artifacts you can provide to demonstrate a tenant wipe (manifests, snapshot deletion logs, storage locator redaction lists), 2) whether backups or snapshots are replicated outside the pinned region and how you prevent that, 3) timeline for complete recovery-free deletion once we issue a wipe, and 4) what audit/exportable logs you can produce for our auditors.

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short plan and the artifacts we can commit to for Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with region pinning. Key points below; attaching our customer-facing wipe playbook (tenant-wipe-playbook-v1.2.pdf) and a small example erase-manifest.

Summary (short):
- Region pinning: Dedicated clusters can be pinned to a single cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) at provisioning. All live tenant storage (model shards, KV caches, ephemeral caches) and primary snapshots remain in-region.
- Backup/replica behavior: By default we disable cross-region snapshot replication for pinned Dedicated deployments. Backups taken by the platform for operational reasons are stored in the same region unless a customer requests multi-region replication in writing.
- Deletion workflow: On tenant-initiated deletion (API call + ticket), we perform a four-step purge: 1) quiesce provisioned nodes -> 2) delete live objects and prefix/KV caches -> 3) expire and securely purge snapshots and block storage volumes -> 4) run a scrubbing job that zeroes object pointers and records a wipe manifest.
- Evidence we can provide: timestamped wipe manifest (CSV or JSON), storage-object deletion logs (object keys and deletion timestamps), snapshot-expiration records, and an exported audit log (syslog/structured JSON) showing the purge run. We can also provide a signed attestation (PDF) from Redwood infra that lists the steps run and the UTC timestamps.
- Timeline: Typical completion depends on dataset size; for most tenants full purge + manifest generation completes within 24–72 hours after the deletion request. Very large stores (multi-TB snapshots) may be longer; we provide an estimated completion window in the deletion ticket and a final manifest when finished.
- Forensic/retention hold: If you require a legal hold or subpoena preservation we can place a paused hold for up to 90 days with documented controls; that is a separate workflow and needs an approved change request.

Next steps I propose:
1) We run a short staging wipe exercise (non-production tenant) and provide the manifest + sample logs — target within 72 hours of your go-ahead.
2) We schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the artifacts and answer auditor questions (I can include Dev and Laura).

Attached: tenant-wipe-playbook-v1.2.pdf (overview of the purge steps) and erase-manifest-example.csv (redacted sample).

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Jane — Laura from Product & Trust here. Quick clarifications to support Sergio's plan and to make sure the audit language is explicit:

1) KMS evidence: We can export key metadata (key id, creation/rotation timestamps, key policy reference) from the cloud KMS for the customer-managed key or our service key. We will include a short mapping table showing which keys protected which snapshots. If you use a customer-managed key, Redwood will not rotate that key without your authorization; we can provide rotation events if requested.

2) Cross-region replicas: Our control plane writes a replication flag into the snapshot metadata. For Dedicated pinned deployments the replication flag is set to "none" by default; we will export snapshot metadata and a cluster-level replication policy as evidence. That metadata is time-stamped and auditable.

3) Post-wipe evidence windows: We will retain the generated wipe manifest and audit export for 180 days by default in our compliance escrow (read-only exports) unless you request a shorter/longer retention window contractually. After 180 days we will purge the escrowed export unless you have an active legal hold.

We can provide formal wording for each of these items (attestation text + metadata sample) as part of the staging run. Sergio — can your team produce the KMS metadata sample and the replication-flag export in the staging deliverable? Dev, can you confirm the 180-day escrow retention default and how customers request changes?

Thanks — Laura Bennett
Head, Product & Trust — Redwood Inference
